NOTICE of Syed Asad Ali (carried as required by Apache-2.0 Section 4(d); file NOTICE_syed3000.txt in the dataset):
  VQCC own-circuit portfolio
  Copyright 2026 Syed Asad Ali. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
  
  Credits: Syed Asad Ali, working with a team of AI agents (GPT-6 Astra Pro, Gemini 4 Argon,
  Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2 and Opus 5.5), with Claude Science supporting the research.
  
  Lineage notice (Apache-2.0, Section 4(d): this NOTICE must be carried by every redistribution):
  - The 46-qubit inverse-square-root generator, the 889-qubit DQI decoder generator (v12 and
    later), and all circuits built from them are the original work of Syed Asad Ali
    (Kaggle: syed3000; dataset syed3000/vqcc-own-circuit-portfolio).
  - This version contains: invsqrt.kmb (44-qubit inverse square root, from that generator line),
    dqi.kmb (890-qubit DQI decoder, from that decoder line), and the chemistry files
    dfthcsos__angle_k_0..14.kmb and dfthcsos__submission.npz (our own loader compiler and word tables).
  - Any redistribution of these files, or of works derived from them at any number of steps
    removed, must include this NOTICE (or its full attribution text) in a readable place, and
    must name "Syed Asad Ali" as the original builder in its credit or lineage line, before
    any later contributors.
  - Improvements by others are welcome; please credit them after the original builder.
NOTICE of marculera (carried as required by Apache-2.0 Section 4; file NOTICE_marculera.txt in the dataset):
  DF-THC 11.38x: (8, 143, 44) table and loaders
  Copyright 2026 marculera (Kaggle)
  
  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (see LICENSE). The weights and words in submission.npz were trained and
  rounded by us from the competition's FeMoCo Hamiltonian, with no public weights or tables. The arrays H1_I and
  Hsym_lower are the hosts' fixed shifts, as published in the starter kit
  (sohier/verifiable-circuit-compilation-starter-kit). No file here is copied from another dataset.
  
  Lineage. If you publish or redistribute this table, its words or its loaders, or anything derived from them (a refit
  of the weights, re-coded words, new loaders on these words), name this dataset, marculera/dfthc-c44-build, as the origin
  and keep this NOTICE with the files, as section 4 of the Apache License requires. The notebook that checks these
  files is https://www.kaggle.com/code/marculera/df-thc-11-38x-codes-on-the-xor-of-five-words
  
  The build rests on public work, credited below as ideas; no code or data of the people named ships here. Each source
  keeps its own terms (some Apache-2.0, some CC0, some "other").
  
  The table
  - Staged progressive rounding, the sign-mixing measure D(w) and the exact gauge refinement of the offsets:
    ahmedberatozer, who credits kozykappa's column rotations and anazemcev's effective-norm method.
  - L-BFGS stages: michaelrustad. One-body refresh from the decoded two-body part: mrmeows.
  - Rounding of an (8, 143, 44) table: the public notes of Syed Asad Ali (syed3000) on his own table
    (vqcc-own-circuit-portfolio).
  - Weight refit at fixed words: phucthaiv02 (joint refit), heliosli and busyaprime (up to the gates), James Barlow
    (manwithacat; constrained refit and gauge rotations), maoxin123 (zero-weight active sets).
  
  The words
  - Coded low bits, one affine pattern per block of 16 addresses, on bit 0 of every word and in some circuits on bit 1
    too: somejoint (qcc-our-chemistry-b143-c60-xor2, Apache-2.0).
  - Codes on the XOR of the five words of a batch, at bits 1 and 2: ours. Placing them on every batch from 3 on: as in
    maoxin123's re-coded tables (QCC v25 to v27).
  
  The loaders
  - Signed Givens gauge (a word's top bit equals the bit below) and the banked QROM that loads ANF deltas: kozykappa,
    Kozykorpesh and Sumit Chongder.
  - Exact lookup emitter design: mrmeows (qcc-1375-open-circuits). Borrowed top bit: heliosli. Five words per circuit:
    heliosli, lightningv08. Padding rows as don't-cares: James Barlow (manwithacat).
  - pi-gauge helper encoding (a word's top bit holds a low address monomial): Atakan Aldemir.
  - Five-block low-monomial plans and exact matroid-parity pair selection: Syed Asad Ali (syed3000), from his published
    circuits and notes. The parity count uses Lovasz's rank formula (L. Lovasz, Matroid matching and some applications,
    J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 28, 1980).
  - The four exact word forms (theta, theta + pi, -theta, pi - theta), the low-block partition and the product pattern
    that fits five dirty words in 128 qubits: gengsr (vqcc-25-2268-portfolio, Apache-2.0).
  - A free padding row in the plans, and the first two loaders, which are based on his published ones: maoxin123
    (qcc-chemistry-4030-toffoli-loaders, CC0).
  - Kernel-relation search in an earlier loader family: qwertykeypadapple.
  
  Our planner and circuit builder are our own code, run on our own words.
  
  The hosts: the official verifier, kickmix and the starter kit.
